narrative:
The model determined that you have a 51% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is just over the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and the type of property you own. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. Only 12.6% of approved applicants are in this situation, while most (59.2%) have no checking account at all. This signaled higher risk to the model.

Your credit history of “no credits or all paid” was the second most important driver and also increased the likelihood of being seen as a bad risk. This category is very rare among approved applicants (only 1%).

The one positive element was that you own real estate. This worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval, but unfortunately it was not enough to overcome the other two factors.

You should focus on improving your checking account balance and building a stronger credit history through consistent, on-time payments. Once these areas look healthier, reapply or explore smaller loan amounts that may be easier to approve.
